resources.string: No server: reachable by address on this network

While this is on, other RemoHop devices can ask to connect to this phone with its ID (or its address on this network) and the temporary password. Every request asks you first, and nobody gets in unless you allow it.

A device you allow sees your screen. It can also tap, swipe and type only if you tick Control in the request, and only while RemoHop\'s accessibility service is on. You can take control away or disconnect it at any time.
Switch Allow remote connection on to accept requests and off to stop. It is off again whenever the app restarts. New password replaces the temporary password; the old one stops working.

Android asks you before your screen is shared. The sharing ends when the last device disconnects, when you tap Stop in the notification or Disconnect here, or when you end it from Android\'s screen sharing indicator.

To be controlled, RemoHop uses an Android accessibility service that you switch on in the system settings. It only performs the taps, swipes, keys and text of a device you allowed with Control, during that session. It reads nothing from the screen for itself. Switch it off in Settings → Accessibility → RemoHop at any time.

RemoHop uses an Android accessibility service so that a device you allow can control this phone: it performs that device's taps, swipes, scrolling, Back, Home and typed text.

It acts only during a remote session you approved with Control ticked, and does nothing at any other time. It does not read, collect or send your screen content or personal data for itself.

You can switch it off at any time in Settings → Accessibility → RemoHop.

Lets a device you allow in RemoHop control this phone: taps, swipes, scrolling, Back, Home and typed text. It acts only during a remote session you approved with Control ticked. It does not read or collect your screen content or personal data. Switch it off here at any time.
